name: EPCIS 2.0.1 event to VSC SEAL mapping under the CBV 2.0 disposition crosswalk (epcis-vsc@2)
notes: The source exchange vectors stay in dpp.interoperability.epcis.v1; this file pins epcis-vsc@2 only. Pinned EPCIS 2.0.1 context 5056c65f991425b1d3a35e35edf4f7d0c7ff56cf688c2912b930f93494713737. Every identifier uses the GS1 demonstration prefix 952 and example.org hosts.

vectors.description: Every CBV 2.0 disposition of section 7.2.3, with the values section 7.2.3.1 deprecates, placed in the same ObjectEvent at the business step other under the actions ADD, OBSERVE and DELETE. The five values CBV shares with the VSC custody model are carried verbatim where the action agrees: active only under ADD, which commissions the objects; in_transit and returned only under OBSERVE; dispensed and destroyed under OBSERVE or DELETE. Every other combination is refused, its reason opening with the mapping limit it cites. A conforming epcis-vsc@2 implementation reproduces each outcome and limit.

The action means what EPCIS 2.0 section 7.4.2 and its siblings say it means for each event type. Only an ObjectEvent whose action is ADD commissions its objects, so only it carries active, the VSC origin: an AggregationEvent, AssociationEvent or TransactionEvent whose action is ADD adds objects that already exist to a parent or a business transaction, and a TransformationEvent carries its inputs, so each reporting active is custody-neutral. A commissioning ObjectEvent can only open the chain, so a transit or terminal disposition on it is a lifecycle-conflict, and so is a transit disposition on a decommissioning ObjectEvent (DELETE); on the other event types ADD and DELETE leave transit and terminal dispositions carried. The transformation action decision is ADD.

The bare, URN and Web URI spellings of one CBV disposition are the same value: each commissioning event maps, the SEAL carries the CBV term, and the round-trip extension keeps the spelling the source used.

A disposition outside CBV 2.0 is refused as non-cbv-disposition under epcis-vsc@2, among them the four VSC-only terms stored, transshipped, transformed and received, which epcis-vsc@1 still maps; a VSC-only term is never written for a CBV event. CBV values are lower case, so Active is not one.

EPCIS 2.0 makes the disposition optional and reads its absence as unchanged. Under epcis-vsc@2 an OBSERVE event without one is custody-neutral (custody-destination-unnamed at a receiving step) and has no SEAL; an ADD or DELETE event without one stays insufficient-data, as under epcis-vsc@1.

vectors.description: A receiving or accepting step whose disposition is neutral, active or absent records a hand-over at the destination, the VSC state Q3, whose only VSC term received is not a CBV disposition: it is refused as custody-destination-unnamed rather than substituted. A receiving step that reports returned is carried as returned; one that reports retail_sold is refused as custody-transition-unnamed.

missing: custody-destination-unnamed: business step "receiving" with disposition "in_progress" records a hand-over at the destination, the VSC state Q3, whose only VSC term received is not a CBV disposition

custody-destination-unnamed: business step "receiving" with disposition "sellable_not_accessible" records a hand-over at the destination, the VSC state Q3, whose only VSC term received is not a CBV disposition
custody-destination-unnamed: business step "accepting" with disposition "active" records a hand-over at the destination, the VSC state Q3, whose only VSC term received is not a CBV disposition
custody-transition-unnamed: disposition "retail_sold" records a custody change for which no VSC term is a CBV value; carrying it fails the SEAL schema and no VSC term is substituted

vectors.description: An event carrying an EPCIS error declaration asserts that the prior event it repeats is in error (EPCIS 2.0 section 7.4.1.2), not that its step happened. epcis-vsc@2 refuses it as error-declaration, so no SEAL asserts the step the source retracted; epcis-vsc@1 maps it with the loss error-declaration, as its manifest publishes. The corrective event is an ordinary event and maps under both. Only a VSC correction retracts a SEAL.

vectors.description: The same events under both mapping profiles. epcis-vsc@1 refuses an observation (an OBSERVE event or a TransformationEvent) at an inspection, repair or sensor reading step that reports active as maintenance-observation, as its manifest publishes, and maps a maintenance step that reports a custody state and an ObjectEvent that commissions its objects. epcis-vsc@2 decides by the custody effect instead: active enters the origin state only on an ObjectEvent that commissions its objects, so every observation reporting active is custody-neutral, whatever its step, and so is a repair recorded as a transformation, whose SEAL would carry objects that already exist. The transformation action decision is ADD.

vectors.description: The five-event document of dpp.interoperability.epcis.v1 (its five-event-document vector carries the same bytes) mapped under epcis-vsc@2 with source references that name epcis-vsc@2. The commissioning ObjectEvent is lossless; the assembling transformations, which report in_progress, and the association, which reports active for a pack the commissioning event already opened, are custody-neutral; the aggregation, transaction and in-transit sensor reading map with their losses named. No SEAL is issued, and nothing touches a token.
